This is exactly the E2 bug. `inject_multi_agent_mode_item`:

```rust
input.retain(|item| !is_multi_agent_mode_item(item));
let insert_at = input
    .last()
    .filter(|item| item.get("role").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("user"))
    .map_or(input.len(), |_| input.len() - 1);
input.insert(insert_at, mode_item);
```

In other words, this developer item is stripped from the history every time and re-inserted **right before the last user message** (or appended at the end if the last item isn't a user message).

Now consider the session flow:
- Turns 1..N: The last item in the history is the real user message → the developer item gets inserted before it. The wire input order: [...history..., developer_item, user_msg].
- At some point the harness pushes a `<system-reminder>` user item after the real user message (e.g., MCP-connection reminder, date rollover, task-completion auto-wake, notification drain — all `push_system_reminder` → user message). Now the last user item is the system-reminder, so the developer item moves to right before the system-reminder item: [...history..., user_msg, developer_item, system_reminder].

This is the swap: the relative order of the developer item and the system-reminder user item has changed. Everything before the swap point stays cached (~10.3k tokens stuck at the pin position), and everything from the swap point onward gets re-written every turn (113–1,004 cache-write tokens per turn until the next cold write / compaction).

Actually, there's an even more subtle point: the developer item is also re-inserted before the last user item every turn. If the last user item stays the same across turns (a tool-result turn: the last item is function_call_output, not a user message), then `insert_at = input.len()` → the developer item goes at the very end. If the last item is a user message (a reminder was just pushed), it goes before it. Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event - you can keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Exit ends the watch.
